question.worked_solution:
To evaluate the given expression, we use PEMDAS.

Notice that ${2}^{-3}=\frac{1}{{2}^{3}}.$ So, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{-3}\times (\frac{8}{5}+4) & = \\ \frac{1}{{2}^{3}}\times (\frac{8}{5}+4) & = \\ \frac{1}{8}\times (\frac{8}{5}+4) & = \\ \frac{1}{8}\times \frac{8+20}{5} & = \\ \frac{1}{8}\times \frac{28}{5} & = \\ \frac{1\times 28}{8\times 5} & = \\ \frac{1\times 4\times 7}{2\times 4\times 5} & = \\ \frac{1\times \cancel{4}\times 7}{2\times \cancel{4}\times 5} & = \\ \frac{7}{10}\end{aligned}
$$
